text: Every night, you fall asleep on an Arabic word... and you don't even know it.
Matrah. Something thrown down: a cushion you throw on the floor, to sit or sleep on.
Its root means to throw. And the ma at the front? The same ma as masjid: the place of. The place you throw yourself down.
Sicily passed it to Italian as materasso... French made it materas... and by the 1300s, English was sleeping on a mattress.
Your turn. The same root is in surah Yusuf, when his brothers plotted against him: itrahoohu. Hide him, sell him, or throw him?
THROW! Kill Yusuf, or throw him out to some land.
So what do you say before you sleep? Comment it!
